transitions.label: Create a task with verification required
Create a task with verification not required

cases.title: Task-created history keeps verify required and not-required as distinct facts
cases.given: A workspace on each supported store (memory, PostgreSQL, and SingleStore) can create tasks through the real task-creation path. One task is created with verification required. A second task is created with verification not required. Each creation records a task-created audit event. Frozen task policy is not changed after creation. Task body size does not determine whether the historical verify-policy fact is kept.
cases.when: Those task-created events are persisted on the event ledger and later read through the event-history consumer on that same backend.
cases.then: For each task, the consumer reports the verify-required or verify-not-required fact that was in force at creation. The two tasks remain distinguishable. Live canonical task and order authority stay intact. Recorded events are not rewritten.
cases.why: After compact task-created events, later consumers still need the creation-time verify policy and cannot recover the required versus not-required distinction from a default.
cases.source: Approved task 261031-136441 Changes and ownership: compact task-created events retain historical policy independent of body size; done criteria require behavioral checks across memory, PostgreSQL, and SingleStore. No policy-preservation AC in req-260802-72fc68; REQ-2 AC-2.5 governs identical work-order context for unchanged lineage only.

setup.text: Memory, PostgreSQL, and SingleStore each have a workspace ready for real task creation.
Can create one task with verification required and one with verification not required.
Reads task-created history after the ledger persists it.

steps.text: Create a task with verification required.
Create a second task with verification not required.

asserts.text: The event-history consumer reports that the first task required verification at creation.
The event-history consumer reports that the second task did not require verification at creation.
Memory, PostgreSQL, and SingleStore all report those same two facts.
The verify-policy fact remains available when the task body is large.
The consumer reports the same verify-policy fact for both tasks.
The historical event replaces live canonical task or order authority.
A recorded task-created event is rewritten.
